record.context_brief: Compare ramification filtrations under monodromy injection
record.original_question: How do the ramification filtrations of Gal(L/K) and Aut_k(X_k) compare under the faithful injection of the finite monodromy group into the automorphism group of the special fiber of the stable model?

evidence.quote: Then Gal(L/K) acts as a group of K-automorphisms on X_L and this action extends as a group of automorphisms to X whose action on the special fiber X_k is faithful: Gal(L/K) -> Aut_k X_k (*)
Question 6.21 How do the ramification filtrations of Gal(L/K) and Aut_k X_k behave under the injection (*)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, and let $X_K$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over $K$ of genus $g\ge 2$. Assume that $X_K$ admits a stable model $X$ over the ring of integers $O_L$ of a finite Galois extension $L/K$, with special fiber $X_k$ (a stable curve over $k$). The Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ (the finite monodromy group of the stable reduction) acts on $X_L:=X_K\otimes_K L$ as a group of $K$-automorphisms, and this action extends to an action on $X$ whose induced action on the special fiber gives a faithful homomorphism
$$\iota:\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)\hookrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}_k(X_k).$$
Both groups carry natural ramification filtrations: $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ has the higher ramification filtration $(G^u)_{u\ge -1}$ (in upper or lower numbering) coming from the local field extension $L/K$, while $\mathrm{Aut}_k(X_k)$ has a ramification filtration arising from the action on the local rings at the singular points and the geometry of the components of $X_k$ in characteristic $p$.

Determine the precise relationship between these two ramification filtrations under the injection $\iota$. In particular, describe how the jumps and successive quotients of the ramification filtration on $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ are reflected in the filtration on its image inside $\mathrm{Aut}_k(X_k)$.
